title: the-cairn-device-owns-the-trouble-panel
intention: The cairn device (singleton, instance 0) owns and surfaces the trouble lane on a web pane. Two-sided: list left, detail right, red light at top (bright red if live, dull reddish grey if none). Starts at row 0. Dynamic page.
why: There is no device that means all-of-Cairn. The trouble lane is a runtime thing with no surface — it is read only at session-open hooks and by hand. A panel that shows live troubles with a red light is the normal-operating-state made visible.
traces_to: Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth. The trouble panel is a diagnostic surface; it shows the full finding, never a summary.
Law 5 — intent, its state, and its proofs share an address. The cairn device's pane is its surface at its address.
I-the-cairn-device.md child a — the cairn device intention names this pane.

falsifier.proves_green: The panel surfaces live troubles from CairnCommons/troubles/ on a web pane declared by the cairn device. TWO sides: list left (trouble id + short summary), detail right (full finding on click). Red light at top: bright red when any trouble is live, dull reddish grey when none. The panel is a PANE on the one web server — it does not own a route, a port, or a server of its own.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) the panel owns its own route/port/server — the one-web-server rule holds, and a device gets a declared PANE, never its own endpoint; (2) the panel does not show live troubles — only showing stale/cached data is not a diagnostic surface; (3) the cairn device is confused with system_rackmount — the host is the laptop, cairn is the project, different scopes, different devices; (4) the trouble detail is truncated or summarized — Law 7 says a diagnostic surface may collapse an error into a coherent shape but the detail view is not a collapse, it is the record; (5) the panel is read-only but does not SAY so — a surface that looks editable but is not is a false affordance.
falsifier.horizon: After the-web-server-graduates-to-starlette — the stdlib web_server is synchronous and cannot do WebSocket push, which the dynamic page needs. This ticket is the Starlette migration's first consumer.

linked_ideas: Akien 2026-08-19, reviewing open questions: trouble tickets are a runtime thing, they need a panel

questions.a: The cairn device is NOT system_rackmount — the host is the laptop, cairn is the project. Different scopes, different devices.
The trouble panel is the cairn device's FIRST pane. Circuit breakers for all devices are the second (child b of the intention, a later ticket).
Dynamic means client-side interaction (click-to-select, live refresh via WebSocket). The current stdlib web_server cannot do this — depends on the Starlette migration.
READ-ONLY surface. No editing or closing troubles from the panel — that is the trouble lane's own door, not a panel's.

how: Build the cairn device (singleton, instance 0) with a trouble-panel web pane. Two-sided: list left, detail right, red light at top. The device means all-of-Cairn and surfaces the trouble lane.

watchme.trigger: a trouble is created or resolved while the panel is serving
watchme.enough: one trouble surfaced on the panel and one resolved, both visible to the operator
watchme.carrier: the trouble record and the panel rendering showing it
watchme.consumer: Akien — the panel must surface troubles he would otherwise have to grep for

CairnCommons/troubles/ — the data source. The trouble store is already read at session-open by the hook; this panel reads the same store.

chart_notes.orient: The trouble store is at CairnCommons/troubles/*.json, already read at session-open by the hook (bin/cmd/session_start_hook). The cairn device is a singleton at instance 0. The pane is a declared shape on the web server, rendered by render.py.
chart_notes.constrain: OUT: editing/closing troubles from the panel (read-only surface); owning a route/port/server (pane on the one web server); showing anything other than the trouble store's own records. IN: the two-sided layout, the red light, the WebSocket push for live updates.
chart_notes.validate: A live trouble appears on the panel within one WebSocket push cycle. The red light is bright red with live troubles, dull reddish grey with none. Clicking a trouble in the list shows its full finding in the detail pane. An empty trouble store shows the dull reddish grey light and an empty list.

filed_edges: Circuit breakers for all devices are the cairn device's second pane (child b of the intention, a later ticket) — not this build.
The trouble store's shape (JSON files in CairnCommons/troubles/) is already settled and not this ticket's to change.
